targets.title: Altair RD-E 2602 Ductile Failure Model
observed_facts: The ZIP contains 20 RAD files: 10 Starter files and 10 Engine files, arranged as three one-shell material checks and seven ruptured-plate variants.
The seven plate Starter decks use /RWALL/SPHER with a 12.7 mm rigid sphere of mass 5 g and an imposed velocity; the projectile has no deformable elements or failure law.
The archive exercises /FAIL/JOHNSON, /FAIL/TAB1 and /FAIL/BIQUAD. It contains no /NONLOCAL card and no embedded measured dataset.
The BIQUAD cards expose Ref.El_Length as zero and the TAB1 cards expose no nonzero element-length function. No objective fracture-energy or characteristic-length regularization is active.
The variants change failure formulations and shell deletion options, not a declared coarse-medium-fine mesh sequence.
official_model_results: Altair presents the case as a numerical comparison of ductile-failure formulations and shell deletion behavior, not as an experimental validation benchmark.

authoritative_primary_provenance.reason: The exact input archive was acquired from the official Altair 2025 endpoint and matched the predeclared content length.

lawful_open_access_and_license.reason: Public download is verified, but no reusable model-file license is embedded; the official documentation page carries an All Rights Reserved notice.

bounded_downloadable_deck_or_reconstruct.reason: The small complete Radioss Starter/Engine decks are present and locally inspectable.

failure_and_regularization_complete.reason: Failure cards are present, but objective regularization is inactive or absent: BIQUAD Ref.El_Length is zero, TAB1 has no active element-length function and no /NONLOCAL card exists.

measured_validation_outputs.reason: The archive contains no measured force, impulse, residual velocity, deformation or perforation dataset.

mesh_and_convergence_definition.reason: The archive contains formulation and shell-option variants, not three documented mesh levels with a common convergence observable.

local_execution_feasible_and_bounded.reason: The small decks are compatible with the available OpenRadioss route and are expected to run within the bounded CPU limit; V9L intentionally does not execute them.

contradictions_and_unknowns: A complete executable deck is useful for software regression but does not supply physical validation.
The projectile is a rigid wall, so the case cannot qualify deformable-deformable contact or projectile rupture.

targets.title: Explicit Finite Element Analysis of 2024-T3/T351 Aluminum Material Under Impact Loading for Airplane Engine Containment and Fragment Shielding
observed_facts: The report documents UCB tests on 12 by 12 inch 2024-T3/T351 aluminum plates with 10 by 10 inch free area, thicknesses 1/16, 1/8 and 1/4 inch, impacted normally by a 1/2 inch 52100 steel sphere.

Measured initial-versus-residual-velocity points are plotted with units for all three thicknesses; approximate ballistic limits are 400, 700 and 1350 ft/s. No uncertainty bars or tabulated measurement uncertainties are supplied.

Both target and projectile are meshed with 8-node solid elements, but the projectile uses linear elasticity only; the report states that the model does not allow projectile plastic yielding and that neither tests nor early runs showed projectile yielding.
The report specifies eroding single-surface contact with SOFT=1 or SOFT=2, matched contact-side element sizes and friction coefficients of 0.5.
Three mesh configurations are documented: Mesh-I at 1/32 inch through-thickness, Mesh-II at 1/64 inch, and Mesh-III at 1/48 inch with a different, denser in-plane pattern.

The Johnson-Cook parameter sets are explicitly tuned to material thickness and element size. The report states that simply refining the mesh does not necessarily improve accuracy and that trial-and-error against controlled test data is used.

A nonlocal failure option is described, but no numeric characteristic length is published for the runs; the report concludes that nonlocal smoothing did not improve accuracy or decrease mesh dependency.
The report supplies no LS-DYNA input deck, complete node/element definition, or model-file reuse terms.
official_model_results: The report compares calculated and measured residual velocity for three plate thicknesses and reports changes from petaling to mixed failure and plugging.

The authors conclude that one parameter set cannot predict the full transition, that parameters tuned for a specific element size are more accurate, and that increased element density did not significantly improve performance.
SOFT=1 and SOFT=2 produced nearly identical results with similar contact mesh densities, while SOFT=2 cost more CPU time.

authoritative_primary_provenance.reason: The inspected report self-identifies as the FAA final report DOT/FAA/AR-08/36 with government sponsorship and public distribution.

lawful_open_access_and_license.reason: The report is public, but no solver deck or explicit model-file reuse license is supplied; report access alone does not license a benchmark deck.

bounded_downloadable_deck_or_reconstruct.reason: Geometry, material tables and contact choices are informative, but the exact meshes, complete boundary/input data and LS-DYNA deck are not published for deterministic reconstruction.

failure_and_regularization_complete.reason: Johnson-Cook damage parameters are listed, but they are calibrated to element size and thickness; the nonlocal length is not numerically fixed and did not remove mesh dependency.

measured_validation_outputs.reason: The report exposes measured initial and residual velocities with units and test geometry for three target thicknesses, although measurement uncertainty is absent.

mesh_and_convergence_definition.reason: Three meshes are compared, but Mesh-III changes the in-plane topology and the study reports sensitivity rather than a converged sequence or numerical uncertainty bound.

local_execution_feasible_and_bounded.reason: The LS-DYNA deck is absent, the solver route is proprietary, and no documented deterministic OpenRadioss conversion is supplied.

contradictions_and_unknowns: This is a strong measured comparator for plate perforation and deformable contact, but not for projectile plasticity or rupture.
The three-mesh comparison is evidence of sensitivity, not evidence that residual velocity or impulse converged.
The graphs expose quantitative points but no measurement uncertainty or raw tables.
